To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) cyclohexanones, isophorones, and phenols are present in a significant amount of aquatic toys and swimming aids, (ii) the concentrations of these compounds vary considerably, (iii) some samples contain very high concentrations of these compounds, and (iv) the presence of these compounds has a significant effect on the odour of the products.
(i) some aquatic toys and swimming aids are contaminated with hazardous organic solvents and (ii) the characteristic odour is predominantly caused by the presence of these solvents.
the concentrations of the three solvents cyclohexanome, isophorome and phenol are significantly elevated in a selection of products obtained from online shops in Germany.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quantification of hazardous organic solutes and their evaluation regarding the odour of the corresponding products.
the determination of hazardous volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in inflatable aquatic toys and the evaluation of their influence with respect to the odour properties of the corresponding product.

the identification and quantification of organic solutes in inflatable aquatic toys and swimming aids and their evaluation regarding their influence on the odour properties of the corresponding devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the odour of the investigated products was predominantly caused by residues from organic solvents.
the odour of the tested products is predominantly caused by cyclohexanones, isophorones, or phenol.
the products analysed in this study contain significant amounts of hazardous organic solvers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the odour of aquatic toys and swimming devices is predominantly caused by cyclohexanones, isophorones, and phenols which are used as additives during the manufacturing process.
the majority of the products contained cyclohexanones, isophorones and/or phenols in concentrations above the respective limit of quantification and thus may be hazardous for the consumer.
the odour of the products is predominantly influenced by the presence of cyclohexaneone and phenol, while the presence of isophorone is not relevant for the overall odour.
The main takeaway from our work is that
some of the aquatic toys and swimming devices investigated contained high amounts of hazardous organic solvolvents.
the odour of inflatable toys for children is mainly caused by the presence of cyclohexane and isophorone as residual solvents.
aquatic toys and swimming aids for children are not necessarily free of hazardous solvents, and that the odour of these products is strongly influenced by their content of organic solvents.
